subject: Atlas Retail — model fit & eval pack / next steps
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Liu <emma.liu@atlasretail.com>
Date: 2026-08-01T09:12:00Z
Subject: Atlas Retail — model fit & eval pack / next steps

Hi Emma — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

Summary of needs
- Primary use: product title & description enrichment + dynamic tag normalization across 20M SKUs.
- Quality target: entity recall >= 94% on key attributes (brand, size, color).
- Latency SLO: p95 < 250ms for production inference.
- Expected throughput: ~400 rps peak (about 24k/min), mostly daytime US peaks.

Initial model recommendations (based on call):
- rw-stable-1-large (recommended starting point for accuracy)
- rw-retail-quant-v2 (8-bit quant) — for cost-optimized inference if latency budget tight
- redwood-1.3-streaming (for low-latency short completion paths)

What I attached / links
- atlas_eval_prompts_v1.csv — curated prompt set reflecting your common failure modes
- atlas_cost_estimate_q3.xlsx — rough cost projection for hosted vs dedicated
- Benchmark report link: https://drive.google.com/drive/fake-link/atlas-eval-pack
- HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/12345678

Recommended next steps
1) Confirm which model(s) you want us to evaluate (we can run rw-stable-1-large + retail-quant-v2).
2) Give us a test dataset (or grant read access to a sample) so we can run the eval pack end-to-end.
3) Schedule a 60-min technical session with Diego (Solutions) to walk through deployment pins and canary strategy.
4) If procurement is needed, share timeline so we can coordinate Dedicated capacity vs hosted commitments.

If you confirm items 1–2 by EOD Wed we’ll aim to deliver an initial eval report within 3 business days.

Thanks — looping in Diego (solutions) to coordinate the tech session.

Best,
Rachel
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
---
Attachments: atlas_eval_prompts_v1.csv, atlas_cost_estimate_q3.xlsx

From: Emma Liu <emma.liu@atlasretail.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@atlasretail.com>
Date: 2026-08-01T11:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Atlas Retail — model fit & eval pack / next steps

Thanks Rachel — this is great, appreciate the summary. A couple quick follow-ups from our side: 

1) We want to prioritize entity recall for brand and size. Important: last week our in-house tests showed a regression after a vendor pushed a model update (v2.1) — entity recall dropped ~6 points on our QA set. Can you document the diff tests we should run to validate no regressions?

2) Procurement is on this thread. They will ask for a list of artifacts we’ll need for our vendor risk assessment (SOC2 evidence, retention policy, data flow diagrams).

3) Timing: we’d like the eval on the rw-stable-1-large first. If that looks good, run retail-quant-v2 to compare cost tradeoffs.

Can we have the eval pack run and a draft report by next Tuesday? Also — if a model update causes regressions in production, what are our options for rollback or pinning?

Thanks,
Emma
Head of Data Product | Atlas Retail

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Liu <emma.liu@atlasretail.com>
Cc: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Procurement <procurement@atlasretail.com>
Date: 2026-08-01T14:22:00Z
Subject: Re: Atlas Retail — model fit & eval pack / next steps

Emma — great questions. Short answers up front, details below:
- Yes, we can run a regression-diff report and hold or pin model versions.
- Canary rollouts are our recommended path for minimizing blast radius.
- We can get an eval packet and draft report to you by Tue (2026-08-04) if we get the sample dataset by EOD Mon.

What rollback/pinning looks like (summary)
- Pin to a specific model artifact/version (e.g., rw-stable-1-large@2026-07-28) — instantaneous routing change, isolated per-customer.
- Canary: route X% traffic to the candidate and keep primary on the stable version; monitor diffs on key metrics (entity recall, precision, latency, token cost).
- If a regression is detected we can shift traffic back to pinned stable within minutes.

Attached: rollback_instructions.md (simple steps we perform + permissions we need). Diego — can you add the specific pin command and a short smoke-test checklist?

Procurement — for vendor assessment we typically provide: SOC 2 Type II summary, data retention policy, overview of private deployment options, and a shared artifact list. I can put together a short package and send it to you by EOD Tue if that helps.

Best,
Rachel

From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Liu <emma.liu@atlasretail.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Procurement <procurement@atlasretail.com>
Date: 2026-08-02T08:40:00Z
Subject: Re: Atlas Retail — model fit & eval pack / next steps

Emma / team — adding the technical details you asked for. Quick checklist and commands below.

Recommended immediate mitigation (if you observed regression in production)
1) Pin production route to the last-known-good model artifact:
   - model pin command (Hosted API): POST /v1/projects/{acct}/routes/{route}/pin with body {"model": "rw-stable-1-large@2026-07-28"}
   - Expected effect: all new inference requests for that route will use the pinned artifact. Reversible.
2) Canary rollout (recommended before wide rollback):
   - Create canary route: 10% -> candidate, 90% -> pinned-stable. Monitor metrics for 24h.

Diff tests to validate regression (we will run these for you)
- Run the attached eval_diff_template.xlsx on your sample set (we’ll populate the report):
  - Per-example outputs from stable vs candidate
  - Token-level distribution diffs
  - Entity extraction recall/precision deltas (brand/size primary)
  - Latency P50/P95 changes

Permissions we need
- A small API key scoped to eval or an S3 link with a 5k sample (CSV) and the ground-truth entity labels.

I can stand up the canary and run the smoke tests — if you approve, I’ll start within 2 business hours once we have the sample. I’ll produce a short diff report and share both the raw outputs + summary.

Attachments: eval_diff_template.xlsx

- Diego
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Emma

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Liu <emma.liu@atlasretail.com>, Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Procurement <procurement@atlasretail.com>, Tom Harris <tom.harris@atlasretail.com>
Date: 2026-08-03T15:40:00Z
Subject: Re: Atlas Retail — model fit & eval pack / next steps

Emma / team — finalizing plan and timeline.

Proposed plan (agreed items)
1) Receive the 5k sample + GT labels (or API key) by COB Mon 2026-08-03.
2) Diego to spin up a 10% canary to rw-stable-1-large@2026-07-28 vs candidate for a 24h smoke test (metrics: brand/size recall, precision, p95 latency).
3) Diego will run the diff report and share the filled eval_diff_template.xlsx within 6 hours of canary completion.
4) If any metric drops by >2 points on entity recall or latency p95 increases by >30%, we will revert traffic to the pinned artifact immediately.

SLA / cost notes
- Canary at 10% is typically negligible vs full rollout; cost delta depends on model size (we estimate a +3–8% cost on the canary window based on mix). We can provide a short credit for the smoke-testing period if procurement needs it — I’ll start the amendment DocuSign for a short-term evaluation credit (link: https://www.docusign.com/en/link/fake-amendment-456).

Next steps for procurement
- I’ll send a vendor package (SOC2 summary, data retention, DI diagram) by EOD Tue. Procurement, please confirm any additional compliance docs you need.

Diego — once you confirm you’re ready, we’ll execute the canary. Emma/Tom — please confirm you’re happy with the 10% canary and timeline.

Thanks all — we’ll move quickly once we have the sample.

Best,
Rachel
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
